concepts.def: Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Withholding information or misleading participants; permitted only if no alternative and harm is minimal.
Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.
Participants must be protected from physical and psychological harm beyond everyday experience.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.
British Psychological Society Code of Ethics and Conduct sets four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Psychology: Issues in Mental Health — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Psychology: Issues in Mental Health brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Psychology: Issues in Mental Health.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many principles does the BPS Code of Ethics contain?
If deception is used, what must be provided afterwards?
options: Debrief
Reward
Public apology
Withdrawal fee

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Because brain scans are unreliable.
Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.
Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.
Strongly nature - behaviours are innate.

mcqs.q: When is deception in research ever acceptable?
options: Always - psychologists can deceive freely.
When demand characteristics would otherwise invalidate the study, with thorough debrief and ethics approval.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
Never - deception is always banned.

mcqs.q: What is the behaviourist view on the nature-nurture debate?
options: Because brain scans are unreliable.
Strongly nurture - we are shaped by environmental conditioning.
Both nature and nurture equally.
Strongly nature - behaviours are innate.
